narrative:
The model predicts you have a 10% chance of failing your final year. While this is a low probability, the system flags it as enough of a risk that you are required to take remedial courses to strengthen your preparation.

The prediction that you might fail is driven mainly by three aspects of your profile. The most influential factor is that you have had no past class failures. Surprisingly, this actually pushes the model toward expecting you to fail. Among students who passed, zero past failures is the average, yet in your specific combination of circumstances the model interprets the complete lack of prior setbacks as a signal that you may not have developed the resilience or study habits needed for final-year demands.

The second strongest influence is that you did not attend nursery school. This pulls the prediction further toward failing. Only 20.7% of students who passed share this background, so the model sees it as a missing early foundation that often correlates with later struggles.

Third, your low amount of free time after school also contributes to the failing prediction. While many passing students report medium or high free time, your lower level suggests you may be overcommitted or lacking balance, making sustained academic effort harder.

To improve, consider building structured study routines, seeking extra support in challenging subjects, and creating healthier boundaries between schoolwork and downtime. These small adjustments can help turn a 10% risk into a clear pass. (248 words)
